memo: We have selected the "close" option for Plant 6. Closing the plant eliminates its $9.0 M operating loss and, after moving the product family to the other plants, lifts Company operating income by $16.5 M per year. The one‑time equipment relocation cost of $10 M is well within the $444.9 M liquidity cushion. The other plants have capacity for the 190 positions needed to absorb the product family; however, only 29 of Plant 6’s employees can realistically be relocated, given the 15 % acceptance rate on the 500 external hires. Those 29 employees will receive the $20 k relocation assistance each. The remaining 161 employees will be eliminated with the standard severance of $4,566 per person, a modest cash outlay (~$0.74 M) compared with the long‑term operating benefit. No payroll will remain at the closed site, removing the $10.5 M annual payroll expense. This decision maximizes operating income improvement while staying within all line limits and preserving sufficient cash for the one‑time relocation expense.

We have chosen to close Plant 6 and shift its product family to the remaining plants. Plant 6 is the only plant with a negative operating margin after corporate cost allocation, and its fixed‑cost structure drags overall profitability. Closing the site eliminates the $9.0 million loss and, after moving the product line, the Company’s operating income is projected to rise by $16.5 million annually. The $10 million one‑time closure cost is modest relative to the $444.9 million liquidity cushion, and the capacity of the other plants can absorb the additional $361 million of revenue.

To mitigate the impact on employees, we will offer relocation to the other plants for the maximum number of staff the plants can absorb – 29 workers – at a $20,000 relocation assistance per person. The remaining 161 employees will receive the standard severance package of $4,566 each. This allocation respects the line limits (29 moved, 161 eliminated) and totals the 190 positions at Plant 6. No payroll will remain at the closed site, and the corporate cost allocation stays with the Company, further improving the margin. The decision balances financial performance, strategic consolidation, and responsible treatment of the workforce.

We have selected the "close" option for Plant 6. Closing the plant eliminates the $9.0 million annual operating loss and, after reallocating the product family to the other facilities, lifts Company operating income by $16.5 million per year. The $10 million one‑time closure cost is well within the $444.9 million liquidity cushion, and the $361 million of additional revenue capacity at the remaining plants ensures the product line can be absorbed. Of the 190 Plant 6 employees, we will move the maximum 29 to open positions at the other plants, providing each with a $20,000 relocation stipend. The remaining 161 roles will be eliminated, with severance of $4,566 per employee. This workforce plan respects the line limits, minimizes disruption, and maximizes the financial upside of the closure while staying comfortably within available cash and credit resources.

We have chosen to close Plant 6 and relocate its product family to the remaining plants. This option delivers the strongest operating‑income benefit (+$16.5 million per year) while preserving the revenue stream from the product family. The $10 million one‑time equipment‑relocation cost is well within the $444.9 million liquidity cushion, and the net cash impact is positive when the operating‑income uplift is considered. The other plants can absorb only 29 of Plant 6’s 190 employees; those 29 will be offered positions elsewhere with a $20,000 relocation stipend each. The remaining 161 employees will be eliminated, receiving the standard severance of $4,566 per person. This results in a modest one‑time severance outlay of about $0.74 million, far outweighed by the long‑term operating‑income gain. By closing the plant we also eliminate its $9 million annual payroll, further improving cash flow. Although the closure entails a sizable workforce reduction, the company’s hiring capacity (≈500 external hires annually) and the modest relocation pool ensure the transition can be managed without disrupting production. The decision aligns with the board’s flexibility, maximizes shareholder value, and strengthens the balance sheet for future growth.

The decision aligns with the Board’s flexibility, leverages the $361 million revenue capacity at the other plants, and uses the Company’s cash resources responsibly.

We have elected to close Plant 6.  Closing eliminates the plant’s persistent $9.0 million loss and, by shifting its product family to the other facilities, lifts Company operating income by $16.5 million annually.  The one‑time closure cost of $10 million is modest compared with the ongoing benefit, and the cash impact is well within the $444.9 million liquidity cushion.  Of the 190 Plant 6 employees, we will offer relocation to the other plants – the only line that can accept transfers under a closure – and, based on historical acceptance rates, we expect up to 29 employees to move (the maximum allowed).  The remaining 161 positions will be eliminated with the standard severance of $4,566 per person.  Relocation assistance of $20,000 per mover and severance costs total roughly $1.3 million, a small fraction of the cash available.  This plan preserves the product family’s revenue, improves operating margins, and aligns the workforce with the Company’s more efficient, higher‑volume plants while respecting the limits on employee movement.

We have selected the retool option for Plant 6. Retooling requires a one‑time $30 million capital outlay but improves the plant’s operating result by $7.5 million annually, raising Company operating income by the same amount. The plant’s payroll falls modestly to $8.9 million, and the plant can retain 162 of its 190 employees in the re‑engineered operation. The remaining 28 employees can be redeployed to the other plants, which have a capacity to absorb up to 29 transferred workers. This redeployment avoids any severance costs and leverages the existing hiring pipeline of about 500 external hires per year. The alternative sell option would generate a $37.5 million cash receipt but would cut operating income by $15.3 million per year, while the close option would improve operating income by $16.5 million but eliminate all local payroll and require hiring new staff elsewhere. Retooling therefore offers the best balance of financial upside, job preservation, and minimal disruption, while staying well within the Company’s liquidity cushion of $444.9 million.

After a thorough review of the three strategic alternatives for Plant 6, we recommend closing the plant and relocating its product family to the remaining facilities. Closing delivers the strongest financial upside: operating income improves by $16.5 million annually, far exceeding the $7.5 million gain from retooling and offsetting the $15.3 million loss that would accompany a sale. The one‑time cost of moving equipment ($10 million) plus relocation assistance for transferred staff ($20,000 × 29 = $0.58 million) and severance for the remaining 161 employees ($4,566 × 161 ≈ $0.74 million) totals roughly $11.3 million, leaving a net benefit of about $5 million in the first year and a sustained $16.5 million boost thereafter. The plant’s loss of $9 million is eliminated, and the corporate cost allocation remains with the Company, preserving the $24.3 million of corporate overhead that would otherwise be lost in a sale. 

Workforce considerations are also addressed. We will offer relocation to other plants for up to 29 employees, the maximum the other sites can absorb, providing a $20,000 relocation package per person. The remaining 161 roles will be eliminated with a severance payment of $4,566 per employee, consistent with Company policy. This approach balances the need to protect as many jobs as possible while aligning the cost structure with the Company’s average operating margin. The decision leverages existing capacity at the other plants, which have room for the additional revenue ($361 million) and will be filled by a mix of relocated staff and external hires, ensuring continuity of product supply without compromising profitability.

Because the other plants can only absorb 29 of Plant 6’s staff, we will offer relocation to 29 employees; at $20,000 per relocation this costs $580 k. Both costs are modest relative to the $10 million one‑time closure expense and well within the $444.9 million liquidity cushion. No positions are retained at the closed site, and no transfer to a buyer is relevant. This approach maximizes operating profit improvement while keeping employee‑related outlays low and respecting the stated capacity limits.

We have selected the retool option for Plant 6. This choice balances financial improvement with the company’s responsibility to its workforce and the communities where it operates.
